title: Weekly Cycle Atlas Edit proposal 2025-06-09
body:
Originating forum post: https://forum.sky.money/t/atlas-edit-weekly-cycle-proposal-week-of-2025-06-09/26608

**Do not merge unless associated poll passes**
author: blimpa
summary: On behalf of @atlas-axis , we are submitting the Atlas Edit Weekly Cycle proposal below. This proposal includes the following edits: Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract - Specifies when the Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process - Provides the Governance Facilitators with greater flexibility in normalizing the effective yield for SKY Token Rewards. Update Spark Artifact And Ecosystem Accord To Prepare For SPK Launch - Updates Spark’s Agent Artifact and one of its Ecosystem Accords to prepare for the SPK launch. Add Timeline For Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract Replace A.4.1.2.2.4.2 - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Portal) / A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Github) to read as follows: A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - MKR To SKY Conversion Emissions (Core) - The legacy MKR to SKY conversion contract (Legacy Conversion Contract) burns MKR and mints new SKY. The new MKR to SKY conversion contract (New Conversion Contract) instead burns MKR and issues SKY from the existing supply of preminted SKY. The Legacy Conversion Contract will be disabled as specified in 4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract. To offset SKY minted by the Legacy Conversion Contract after the deployment of the New Conversion Contract, an equivalent amount of preminted SKY will be burned. This action will ensure the total SKY token supply remains as if these specific emissions from the Legacy Conversion Contract had not occurred. A.4.1 - Core Tokens - SKY - Disabling Legacy Conversion Contract (Core) - The disabling of the Legacy Conversion Contract will be executed in the June 26, 2025 Executive Vote. This action is authorized to proceed directly to an Executive Vote without a prior Governance Poll. Refine SKY Rewards Rate Normalization Process Replace A.4.3.2.1 - SKY Token Rewards (Portal) / A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Github) to read as follows: A.4.3 - Savings Rate And Token Reward Mechanism - Token Reward Mechanism - SKY Token Rewards (Core) - With each Executive Vote, the distribution of SKY token rewards to USDS holders is normalized to ensure the effective yield provided by these rewards equals the Sky Savings Rate (SSR) for the upcoming period. The effective yield is defined as: (Total Market Value of Distributed SKY Tokens / Total Eligible USDS Balance). To achieve this normalization, the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed is determined through the following calculation, performed for each normalization period: Determine Target Reward Value: Calculate the total US dollar value required to meet the SSR for the period: (Total Eligible USDS Balance * SSR). Determine SKY Token Quantity: Divide the Target Reward Value (from step 1) by the Current Market Price of SKY (determined at the time of the Executive Vote). The Governance Facilitators, on the recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors, may maintain the quantity of SKY token rewards to be distributed for a normalization period at its current level if they conclude that: the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Tokens Rewards and the SSR is not material; the difference between the effective yield provided by SKY Token Rewards and the SSR is unlikely to persist due to other factors; or adjusting the quantity of SKY Token Rewards is otherwise inadvisable. The recommendation of the Stability Scope Advisors must be posted to the Sky Forum and approved by the Stability Facilitators. Update Spark Artifact And Ecosystem Accord To Prepare For SPK Launch Delete A.2.9.1.2.2.2.1.2.2 - Liquidity For Market Makers Stipulation (Portal) / A.2.10 - Liquidity For Market Makers Stipulation (Github) Replace A.2.9.1.2.2.5.4 - Initial Allocation Mechanism (Portal) / A.2.10 - Initial Allocation Mechanism (Github) to read as follows: Initial Allocation Mechanism ( Core ) - Shortly after the Agent Token launch, an Atlas Edit Proposal submitted to Sky Governance will allow the respective founding teams of Spark and Launch Agent 1 to propose an initial cash grant to their respective Star Foundation. Sky Governance must consent to this initial cash grant via approving the Sky Atlas modification. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P1.3.1.1.4 - Custom Instance Parameters (Portal) / Spark - Custom Instance Parameters (Github) to read as follows: Spark Foundation (Core) - The Spark Foundation is the Star Foundation associated with Spark. Its mandate is to support the development, growth, and adoption of Spark. Phoenix Labs (Core) - Phoenix Labs is a development company that provides services to the Spark Foundation. Phoenix Labs is a “Nested Contributor”, i.e., a core contributor to both Spark and Sky. Add new subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.1.7 - Custom Instance Parameters (Portal) / Spark - Custom Instance Parameters (Github) to read as follows: Staking (Core) - SPK token holders can stake their tokens. The rewards for staking will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.1.P4.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) to read as follows: Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd (Core) - The Genesis Supply was minted to an account owned by SPK Company Ltd. The address of the account on the Ethereum Mainnet is 0x6FE588FDCC6A34207485cc6e47673F59cCEDF92B . Transfer Of Tokens To Sky (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 6.5 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Sky Pause Proxy. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. Transfer Of Tokens To Spark SubProxy Account (Core) - SPK Company Ltd transferred 918,760,451 SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark SubProxy Account. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The Spark SubProxy Account is specified in SubProxy Account . Transfer Of Tokens To Spark Foundation (Core) - SPK Company Ltd will transfer 1 billion SPK tokens from the SPK Company Ltd account to the Spark Foundation. The SPK Company Ltd account is specified in Minting Of Tokens To SPK Company Ltd. The address of the Spark Foundation on the Ethereum Mainnet will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Tokens Retained By SPK Company Ltd ( Core) - 1,581,239,549 SPK tokens will be retained by SPK Company Ltd. The use of these tokens will be specified in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. Replace the subdocuments of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.1 - Routine Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Routine Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Root Edit Proposal Submission (Core) - The Root Edit process begins with a SPK token holder submitting a proposal through the Powerhouse system containing a draft Artifact Edit Proposal. A SPK token holder must hold at least 1% of the total token supply to submit a proposal. The proposal must also be posted on the Sky Forum under the “Spark” tag. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Nested Contributors (Core) - Nested Contributors are always authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and do not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. To see the Agent’s Nested Contributors, see Phoenix Labs. Root Edit Proposal Submission Requirements Exception For Spark Foundation (Core) - While it is a core service provider to Spark, the Spark Foundation is authorized to submit Artifact Edit Proposals and does not have to fulfill the token-holding requirements defined in Root Edit Proposal Submission. However, all other procedural requirements within the Root Edit process continue to apply. Short-Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports submitting Artifact Edit Proposals, SPK token holders may submit Artifact Edit Proposals by posting them to the Sky Forum under the “Spark” category. The title of the post must include the text “Spark Artifact Edit Proposal”. The post must include cryptographic proof that the author controls an account holding the required percentage of the total SPK token supply specified in Root Edit Proposal Submission. Root Edit Expert Advisor Review (Core) - A future iteration of the Spark Artifact will specify guidelines for obtaining specialized review of proposals requiring advanced technical or financial analysis. Root Edit Proposal Review By Operational Facilitator (Core) - Within seven (7) days of the proposal being submitted, the Operational Facilitator must review the Root Edit Proposal for alignment. If the proposal is aligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding. In this Forum post, the Operational Facilitator must also confirm that the proposal is feasible for Operational GovOps to operationalize. If the proposal is misaligned, the Operational Facilitator must respond to the Forum post to announce their finding and provide the reasoning for it. Root Edit Token Holder Vote (Core) - Where their review of the proposal results in a finding of alignment with the Sky Core Atlas and Spark Artifact, the Operational Facilitator next triggers a Snapshot poll to allow token holders to vote on the proposal. The poll is open for three (3) days. A poll must have at least 10% of the circulating token supply participating and must have 50% of votes in favor to be approved. Circulating Supply Definition (Core) - For purposes of Root Edit Token Holder Vote, the circulating supply of SPK tokens is equal to the total supply of SPK tokens minus the sum of: Tokens retained by SKY and not yet distributed as token rewards (see A.2.10 - Sky Retained Tokens And Reward Pools ); and Tokens retained in vesting agreements for Spark contributors and not yet distributed; and Tokens in the Spark SubProxy Account (see SubProxy Account ). Root Edit Artifact Update (Core) - At the conclusion of the poll, if the proposal is approved, the Operational Facilitator submits the edit to Powerhouse to formally update the Agent Artifact. Regardless of the outcome, the Operational Facilitator updates the Powerhouse System to include the result of the vote, including any pertinent documents. Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - Until the Powerhouse system supports updating Agent Artifacts, the Operational Facilitator works with the Governance Facilitators to update the Atlas GitHub repository located at Pull requests · sky-ecosystem/next-gen-atlas · GitHub to reflect proposals approved by Star Governance. Artifact Edit Restrictions (Core) - The Spark Artifact cannot be edited in any way that violates the Sky Core Atlas or its specifications of the Sky Primitives, or in any way that is otherwise misaligned. The Operational Facilitator must enforce this rule through their review of Artifact Edit Proposals. Time-Limited Root Edit Restrictions On Removal Of Nested Contributors (Core) - For a period of three years after June 4, 2025, any Artifact Edit that would have the effect of removing a Nested Contributor must be approved by a vote of SKY holders in addition to a vote of SPK holders to be effective. Add a new subdocument of A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2 - Operational Process Definition (Portal) / Spark - Operational Process Definition (Github) This document should be located directly after A.AG1.2.2.P6.2.1.2.3 - Emergency Protocol (Portal) / Spark - Emergency Protocol (Github) to read as follows: Short Term Transitionary Measures (Core) - In the short term, the parameters of the Spark Liquidity Layer, SparkLend, and Spark Savings are controlled by Sky Core, but will be transitioned to Spark in a future iteration of the Spark Artifact. See SparkLend Risk Parameters Modification .
